o: Explain when a computer needs virtual memory.
Describe how the operating system moves pages between RAM and secondary storage.
Explain why heavy use of virtual memory reduces performance.
c: RAM is the computer's working space. When active programs need more working memory than physical RAM can hold, the operating system may move less-used pages to secondary storage.
The operating system uses a reserved area of secondary storage as extra backing space for memory pages.
Pages are moved between RAM and secondary storage as needed; this is substantially slower than accessing RAM.

Virtual memory helps the system continue working when RAM is insufficient, but frequent transfers to/from slower secondary storage reduce performance. Never say that virtual memory is a type of cache.

m.title: Virtual Memory · worked example
m.q: A laptop needs 6 GB for active programs but has only 4 GB available RAM. Explain what virtual memory does and why performance may fall. [4 marks]
st: 6 GB is needed but only 4 GB of physical RAM is available.
The OS can use some secondary storage as backing for inactive pages.
Accessing secondary storage is slower; swapping pages frequently slows the system. [4]

w: A laptop opens many browser tabs. Explain why virtual memory might be used. [3]
The total working memory demand may exceed RAM [1]; the OS temporarily stores less-used pages on secondary storage [1] and brings them back when needed [1].
Explain why adding RAM could reduce use of virtual memory. [3]
More active data fits in physical RAM [1], reducing page transfers to secondary storage [1] and therefore decreasing slow accesses [1].
A student says virtual memory makes a laptop faster than RAM. Evaluate the statement. [4]
Virtual memory extends apparent working capacity [1] and can allow more programs to remain open [1], but its secondary-storage backing is slower than RAM [1], so heavy paging reduces performance [1].

k.q: Predict whether the memory check reports extra storage is needed.
k.code:
neededGB = 6
freeRAMGB = 4
if neededGB > freeRAMGB then
    print("Virtual memory needed")
else
    print("RAM sufficient")
endif
p: Extend to output the shortage in GB.

priorExam.q: Explain the difference between RAM and ROM in terms of purpose and volatility. [4]
priorExam.a: RAM holds current programs and data [1] and is volatile [1]. ROM holds firmware/startup instructions [1] and is non-volatile [1].

stretch.task: Extend Code First so that it also prints the shortage in GB when extra storage is needed. Test 6 GB needed against 4 GB and then 8 GB free RAM.
stretch.hint: Within the first branch, subtract freeRAMGB from neededGB; avoid reporting a negative shortage.
stretch.answer: At 6 GB needed and 4 GB free, it prints Virtual memory needed and 2 GB shortage. At 8 GB free, it prints RAM sufficient and no shortage.

mastery.task: A school computer runs tasks needing 2 GB, 3 GB and 4 GB, with 7 GB of available RAM. Adapt your program to total the three values, check for a shortage, and explain why any secondary-storage backing could slow the system.
mastery.hint: Total demand = 2+3+4. Compare this with 7; then connect page movement to storage speed.
mastery.answer: Demand = 9 GB, free RAM = 7 GB, shortage = 2 GB. The program reports extra memory needed. Moving pages between RAM and secondary storage creates slower accesses because secondary storage is slower than RAM.
